# Leslie Moore

## Overview

- **Age:** 28 years old  <sub>[v4 c10 P49](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0049), [v4 c13 P15](../source/v04-c13.md#nw-v04-c13-p0015)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v4 c8 P17](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0017), [v4 c10 P10](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0010)</sub>
- **Status:** Engaged to be married at Christmas  <sub>[v4 c40 P11](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0011)</sub>
- **Origin:** Four Winds  <sub>[v4 c11 P4](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0004), [v4 c11 P15](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0015)</sub>
- **Role:** Keeps summer boarders; former schoolteacher  <sub>[v4 c11 P22](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0022), [v4 c26 P3](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0003)</sub>
- **Titles:** Mrs. Moore  <sub>[v4 c8 P17](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0017)</sub>; Mrs. Dick Moore  <sub>[v4 c10 P10](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0010)</sub>

## Appearance

Leslie is a remarkably beautiful and slender woman with milk-white skin, an ivory-tinted neck and arms, and striking sea-blue or shining gray-green eyes. She has a splendid head of long golden hair that gleams like molten gold in the light and falls to her feet when unloosed. Her hands are brown and work-hardened, and she is known for her vibrant, graceful figure and customary accent of a red flower or crimson scarf about her attire.

_Sources: [v4 c8 P17](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0017), [v4 c11 P15](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0015), [v4 c12 P5](../source/v04-c12.md#nw-v04-c12-p0005), [v4 c12 P21](../source/v04-c12.md#nw-v04-c12-p0021), [v4 c21 P17](../source/v04-c21.md#nw-v04-c21-p0017), [v4 c23 P24](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0024), [v4 c26 P18](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0018), [v4 c38 P1](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0001)_

## Personality

Leslie possesses a glowing, intensely emotional nature beneath a facade of initial coldness, bitterness, and reserve forged by years of tragedy. She holds a fiercely rigid sense of duty and determination, stoically keeping her grievances to herself while carrying heavy obligations without complaint. Though she is not widely social, she exhibits an eager, starved soul that blossoms into quick wit, laughter, warmth, and deep loyalty when surrounded by loving companionship.

_Sources: [v4 c8 P17](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0017), [v4 c11 P13](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0013), [v4 c12 P5](../source/v04-c12.md#nw-v04-c12-p0005), [v4 c21 P13](../source/v04-c21.md#nw-v04-c21-p0013), [v4 c23 P24](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0024), [v4 c25 P15](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0015), [v4 c30 P27](../source/v04-c30.md#nw-v04-c30-p0027), [v4 c31 P0](../source/v04-c31.md#nw-v04-c31-p0000)_

## History

Leslie West grew up in Four Winds, enduring severe family tragedies in her youth, including the death of her beloved brother Kenneth and the suicide of her father Frank West. Inheriting funds from her grandmother, she completed two years of work in one at Queen's Academy and became a teacher at Glen school. At sixteen, she was coerced into marrying Dick Moore to save her mother's mortgaged farm from foreclosure. Soon after her mother died, Dick went to sea and disappeared, only to be brought back years later mentally incapacitated, leaving Leslie to nurse him in poverty and isolation. After meeting Anne Shirley Blythe, Leslie formed a deep, enduring friendship that transformed her life and restored her spirits. When writer Owen Ford visited Four Winds, he and Leslie fell secretly in love. Out of a strict sense of duty, Leslie agreed to send the brain-injured man she believed to be Dick to Montreal for surgery; the operation revealed that the man was actually his double cousin George Moore, freeing Leslie from her marriage ties. Following this revelation, Leslie accepted Owen Ford's proposal of marriage in the garden, with plans to wed at Christmas.

## Background by volume

- Daughter of Frank West and Rose Elliott  <sub>[v4 c11 P15](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0015)</sub>
- Witnessed the traumatic accidental death of her four-year-old brother Kenneth when she was twelve  <sub>[v4 c11 P16](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0016)</sub>
- Discovered her father's body after he hanged himself when she was fourteen  <sub>[v4 c11 P20](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0020)</sub>
- Inherited money from her grandmother West to attend Queen's Academy, finishing two years of study in one  <sub>[v4 c11 P22](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0022)</sub>
- Taught at the Glen school prior to her marriage  <sub>[v4 c11 P22](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0022)</sub>
- Forced into marrying Dick Moore at age sixteen to prevent foreclosure on her mother's farm  <sub>[v4 c10 P49](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0049), [v4 c11 P26](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0026)</sub>
- Lost her mother to pneumonia a year after her marriage  <sub>[v4 c11 P28](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0028)</sub>
- Distantly related to the West family of Ellen and Rosemary West  <sub>[v5 c2 P66](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0066)</sub>

## Quotes

> I am Leslie Moore—Mrs. Dick Moore  <sub>[v4 c10 P10](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0010)</sub>

> I ENVY Anne, and I’d envy her even if she had died! She was a mother for one beautiful day. I’d gladly give my life for THAT!  <sub>[v4 c19 P28](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0028)</sub>

> There is no cage. But—it doesn’t seem as if there were anything else, Anne. You—you remember what I told you of my folly that night on the sand-bar? I find one doesn’t get over being a fool very quickly. Sometimes I think there are people who are fools forever. And to be a fool—of that kind—is almost as bad as being a—a dog on a chain.  <sub>[v4 c33 P14](../source/v04-c33.md#nw-v04-c33-p0014)</sub>

> Anyhow, I have YOU. Life can’t be altogether empty with such a friend. Anne, pat my head—just as if I were a little girl—MOTHER me a bit—and let my tell you while my stubborn tongue is loosed a little just what you and your comradeship have meant to me since that night I met you on the rock shore.  <sub>[v4 c33 P17](../source/v04-c33.md#nw-v04-c33-p0017)</sub>
